body:
DESIGN CHECKPOINT — bd-01M158ACR8F9X3BA3HG7CVRKZ6, no edits yet.

Read: FeatureDerivation.canonicalString/derivationId/outputSpaceId (derivation.scala:125-151); Windowed.apply / overBasis / Aggregate.overTargets all stamp space.id from d.outputSpaceId (window.scala:315-328); TrackProvenance is (Provenance, Option[storyChecksum]) only (track.scala:17-20); no in-module cache keyed on derivationId (DerivationGraph keys on FeatureSpaceId). GoldenDerivationId pins derivationId, not the space id.

Proposed shape:

1. BasisId — opaque checksum. Canonical render is kind + ordered FeatureTargetKey.parts of the basis units, nothing else (not supports, not estimates). Kinds: situations | segments | targets (overTargets that is not a NarrativeBasis). Order is the caller's order; permutation ⇒ different id. Empty basis still has a kind, so empty-situations ≠ empty-segments.

2. derivationId — unchanged. canonicalString does not mention the basis. GoldenDerivationId and FeaturesCodecSuite derivationId round-trip stay put.

3. outputSpaceId — FeatureDerivation.outputSpaceId stays the no-basis form (derived: + derivationId.short(32)) so surface Windowed.apply and existing single-target recipes do not move. New overload outputSpaceId(basis: BasisId) = derived: + Checksum.ofText(derivationId.hex + "|" + basis.hex).short(32). Length stays 8+32. Windowed.overBasis / Aggregate.overBasis / Aggregate.overTargets use the overload.

4. Provenance — TrackProvenance gains basisId: Option[BasisId] (None on raw and surface-window tracks). That is a new wire field. I will not touch codec/features.scala until you or Codex-root ok the field; if you want the field deferred, I can keep BasisId on the space id only for this slice.

5. Cache — no features cache to retarget. DerivationGraph.add already keys on the output FeatureSpaceId, so once that id includes the basis, two same-recipe/different-basis tracks cannot share an edge.

Laws I will add (features tests; StructureSuite/WindowSuite not yet reserved): same recipe + different basis ⇒ different outputSpaceId; same units in a different order ⇒ different BasisId; no-basis outputSpaceId and derivationId goldens unchanged.

One question: is overTargets' kind "targets" correct, or should it reuse the TargetFamily of the head (situation/segment/surface-unit) so two situation lists cannot collide with a "targets" spelling of the same ids? I favor encoding the actual family when all units share one, and rejecting mixed families (already rejected at window.scala:435-437).

Holding code until you flag this.
